chunks: He narrated to me: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from his father Isma'il from Ibn Muskān from Abi al-Sāmit who said:
Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: One prayer in the Mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him) equals ten thousand prayers.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for prayer in the Mosque of the Prophet according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent Qummi chain in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the unique spiritual status of the Prophet’s Mosque (Masjid al-Nabi) as a locus of divine grace. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical sanctity of the Ahl al-Bayt’s resting places, where worship yields multiplied rewards due to the proximity to the Prophet’s legacy. This specific multiplier of ten thousand highlights the exceptional merit of performing obligatory or supererogatory prayers in this sacred space compared to other mosques.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from his father, from Ibn Muskān, from Abī Sāmit, who said:
Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: One Salāt in the Mosque of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) is equal to ten thousand Salāt elsewhere.
